articles.title: Uniswap V4 Security Guide: Hooks, Pools, and New Attack Vectors You Need to Know Before Deploying
articles.excerpt: Uniswap V4 hooks are the most powerful primitive ever shipped in AMM design — and the most dangerous. One misconfigured hook can drain an entire pool in a single transaction, and with over $1B in TVL…
articles.body: Uniswap V4 hooks are the most powerful primitive ever shipped in AMM design — and the most dangerous. One misconfigured hook can drain an entire pool in a single transaction, and with over $1B in TVL migrated from V3 within weeks of launch, there's a lot of money sitting behind code most people haven't audited. I've gone through the V4 architecture, the PoolManager contract, and a stack of early hook implementations. The vulnerability surface isn't just new — it's fundamentally different from anything that came before. How Hooks Change the V4 Security Model Uniswap V4 moves all pools into a single singleton contract called PoolManager . Instead of deploying a new pair contract per token pair (V2/V3 style), every pool lives in one contract and is identified by a PoolKey struct.
articles.author: Duron Epps

articles.body: A realistic, activity-by-activity estimate — plus how to measure your own usage and cut it down Disclosure: this article is written by the NXTL team. NXTL makes a travel eSIM, which we mention briefly below. "How many gigabytes do I need for two weeks in Spain?" is one of the most common travel questions, and the honest answer is: it depends almost entirely on what you do with your phone. A traveller who navigates and messages might get by on a few hundred megabytes a week. One who uploads Stories and takes video calls every evening can burn through several gigabytes. Below is a breakdown by activity. All figures are rough estimates. Real usage varies with app versions, video quality settings, network speed, and how much of your phone's background activity you allow.

articles.body: 问题：AI 不认识小商家 问大模型“堪察加有什么火山徒步线路、下周有没有位置”，它一般会给你一段概括性的介绍，然后建议你“联系当地旅行社”。原因很简单：堪察加的旅行社大多是几个人的小团队，信息散在俄语网站、Telegram 频道和电话里，搜索引擎抓不全，模型训练数据里更没有实时的余位和价格。 我们做的 Vedar（vedarai.ru）是堪察加本地的旅行平台，汇总了当地旅行社的线路、包车、租车和住宿。网站本身对人是友好的，但我们发现越来越多的用户在用 AI 助手规划旅行，于是决定把平台直接开放给 AI 智能体——用的就是 MCP（Model Context Protocol）。 架构：一个远程 MCP 服务器 接入地址： https://vedarai.ru/api/mcp 传输：Streamable HTTP 鉴权：无（查询类全部只读） 文档： https://vedarai.ru/mcp 仓库： https://github.com/tourhabk-ui/vedar-mcp （有中文 README） 我们没有让 MCP 去爬自己的网页，而是让工具直接读平台的业务数据：线路目录、实时余位、合作方的住宿和车辆。这样 AI 拿到的价格和日期就是旅行社在后台维护的那一份，不会出现“网页改了、AI 还在说旧价格”的问题。 22 个工具，分三类 tools/list 当前返回 22 个工具： 1.

articles.title: Go Runtime Choices for AI Models and Better Linguistic Nuance in EU Support Chatbots
articles.excerpt: TL;DR: For an EU customer-support chatbot that must return valid structured answers from a private knowledge base, I would start with Claude and accept the latency tradeoff. OpenAI chat models are the…
articles.body: TL;DR: For an EU customer-support chatbot that must return valid structured answers from a private knowledge base, I would start with Claude and accept the latency tradeoff. OpenAI chat models are the better default when response speed and generality dominate. Keep the choice reversible: query /v1/models , record the selected model and vendor, validate every response against your schema, and make a retry incapable of duplicating a support action. The operational constraint changes the answer. A fluent paragraph is not enough when the client expects {answer, citations, escalation_required} and a malformed object sends a customer down the wrong path. Linguistic nuance matters across EU languages, but a parser failure is still an incident.

articles.title: I Was Too Lazy to Open Five AI Tabs, So I Built AgentWebUI 🦥
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady Did you know the chainsaw was originally invented to help with childbirth? Two Scottish doctors in the late…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady Did you know the chainsaw was originally invented to help with childbirth? Two Scottish doctors in the late 1700s looked at a hard, slow, painful job and thought: there has to be a lazier way. A few centuries later, we use it to cut down trees and star in horror movies. That's the thing about laziness. It's not a character flaw. It's the R&D department of the human race. So here's my confession. My AI workflow had become a part-time job. Claude Code in one terminal. Codex in another. A local Llama in Ollama. DeepSeek in a browser tab I kept losing. Every task started with the same ritual: which tab was I in, and where did I put that conversation? OpenWebUI was supposed to fix this.

articles.title: Break It on Purpose
articles.excerpt: An AI pipeline that catches its own bugs, explains them, and fixes them while a human makes two decisions. By Denis Zontak, written with Claude. Originally published at zontakllc.com. At 17:45 on Octo…
articles.body: An AI pipeline that catches its own bugs, explains them, and fixes them while a human makes two decisions. By Denis Zontak, written with Claude. Originally published at zontakllc.com . A bug in the search box At 17:45 on October 24, 2026, the search box on our staging site started to crash. We had put the bug there on purpose: one line in a database read skipped archived clients, so a search that found their entries failed with Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name') . Nobody told the system. Forty-two seconds after the first error, a fix request was waiting in our pipeline. Thirty-one minutes after the first error, a pull request was ready for review: a one-line fix, and a test that proves it. A person made two decisions in between.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 24, 1946: V-2 rocket takes 1st photos of Earth from space
articles.excerpt: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. While these grainy, black-and-white images might not look like much today, they were a huge deal at the time, because no one had ever seen Earth from space before. The V-2 rocket launched from the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. It carried a 35-millimeter motion picture camera that captured a new frame every second and a half. The rocket soared to an altitude of about 65 miles before falling back to Earth. Both the rocket and the camera were destroyed after crashing into the Earth at a speed of about 340 miles per hour. But the film survived because it was protected inside a steel case. Scientists had to drive out into the New Mexico desert to retrieve the film.

articles.title: 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' was afraid to say anything in season of gimmicks
articles.excerpt: The fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was one giant gimmick: shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres.
articles.body: It didn’t take long for fans to figure out that the fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was going to be unlike any season of " Star Trek " before it. The entire season was one giant gimmick, and that gimmick was shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres. You could argue that an entire season of gimmick episodes is a bold risk: putting the characters in fun, wacky situations to see how they react. It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. It was all so safe and paint-by-numbers, and, most importantly, it didn't have anything profound or interesting to say. That should trouble any Trekkie.

articles.title: Medusa's eye, Halloween fireballs and more: 5 skywatching targets to look out for this spooky season
articles.excerpt: Five spooky skywatching targets perfect for naked eye stargazing this Halloween!
articles.body: The spooky season is officially here! To celebrate, we've put together a list of five Halloween-themed skywatching targets that you can enjoy with nothing but the naked eye or binoculars and, of course, clear skies. Over millennia, the night sky has helped shape human beliefs. In return, we have imprinted our myths, stories and perceptions upon it, seeing monsters and mythology in the twinkling lights of the stars and assigning sinister aspects to innocent cosmic objects. Many of these ghostly impressions and meanings have survived to the present day. Here are a few of our favorites. The Pleiades open star cluster Don't be fooled by their beauty; the blue-white stars of the Pleiades are dripping in spooky lore.

articles.title: SpaceX launches Starlink satellites from California as Falcon 9 cadence slows (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX sent 27 more of its Starlink broadband satellites to orbit today (Oct. 23), in its first Starlink launch in 11 days.
articles.body: SpaceX launched its newest batch of Starlink broadband internet satellites today (Oct. 23) from the California coast. The spacecraft, Starlink Group 15-15, were stacked 27 high inside the payload fairing of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket , which lifted off from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 6:48 p.m. EDT (2248 GMT; 3:48 p.m. local time in California). The rocket's first stage booster, designated B1063, executed its main engine cutoff and stage separation about 2.5 minutes into flight, sending the second stage to continue onward to low Earth orbit (LEO). The vehicle's two-piece protective payload fairing was jettisoned just before T+3 minutes. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches 27 Starlink satellites from California on Oct. 23, 2026.
